answer.title: Loan events, a status transition function and a reminder consumer Lambda
answer.summary: The PR adds a `LoanEvent`/`Queue` module, a `transition()` function in `status.py`, a `consumer.py` Lambda and a SAM template. It also adds a front desk `POST /remind` route. The wiring does not meet the acceptance criteria. Reminders are mailed twice (once by `send_reminders`, once by the consumer). `publish_overdue` always raises. Events have no id and no dedup. The front desk imports and calls the consumer. `Queue` is only an in-memory list, so no event reaches SQS.
answer.behavior: Today `send_reminders` mails members directly. After this PR it also publishes `loan.reminded`, and the consumer mails the member again, so each member gets two reminder mails. The overdue publisher fails on the first loan it processes. The front desk gets a `/remind` route that sends the mail synchronously from the front desk Lambda.

merge_risk.why: Duplicate member mails, an always-failing overdue job, no event delivery to SQS, and a template that may leave the front desk token empty.

effort.why: Several files, but each is small. The real work is checking the control flow across producer, queue and consumer against the acceptance criteria.

rule_checks.rule: Every status change goes through status.py only
rule_checks.why: The consumer sets `reminded_on` directly, and the existing `LoanStore.give_back` (library/loans.py:41) sets `returned_on` directly.

rule_checks.rule: Consumer is the only sender of reminder/overdue mails
rule_checks.why: `send_reminders` still calls `mailer.send`, and the front desk `/remind` route calls `consumer.handle`.

rule_checks.rule: Lambdas share only the events module
Events carry an id and the consumer dedups
rule_checks.why: `LoanEvent` has no id and the consumer keeps no record of handled events.

rule_checks.rule: Exactly one reminder mail two days before due
rule_checks.why: A direct send plus a consumer send gives two mails.

nodes.label: Front desk staff (HttpApi)
nodes.description: Calls GET /late and POST /remind with a bearer token.

nodes.label: handler (handler.py)
nodes.details:
The front desk Lambda entry.
- **New `/remind` route** that calls `consumer.handle` directly.
- **Imports `consumer`**, so the consumer code ships with the front desk.

nodes.label: consumer (consumer.py)
nodes.details:
Reads SQS records and mails the member.
- **`handle`** mails for `loan.reminded` and `loan.overdue`.
- **Sets `reminded_on` directly**, outside `status.py`.
- No dedup.

nodes.label: reminders (reminders.py)
nodes.description: Finds loans to remind and publishes overdue events.
nodes.details:
Finds loans due soon and overdue loans.
- **`send_reminders`** now also calls `transition`, but still mails directly.
- **`publish_overdue`** is new and always raises.

nodes.label: status (status.py)
nodes.details:
The loan status state machine.
- **`transition()`** validates the move, updates the loan and publishes a `LoanEvent`.

nodes.label: events (events.py)
nodes.details:
The event type and a queue wrapper.
- **`Queue.publish`** only appends to a list.
- **`LoanEvent`** has no id.

nodes.label: LoanEvents (SQS queue)
nodes.description: The queue between the two Lambdas.

context.relation: `api.store` is the in-memory store the consumer reads.
The Mailer is used by both `send_reminders` and the consumer.

steps.title: Events and the status transition
steps.why_it_matters: This is the single place that should change status and publish events, and the acceptance criteria hang on it.
steps.explanation: Adds `LoanEvent` and a list-backed `Queue`. Adds `transition()`, which validates via `move`, mutates the loan and publishes an event. The event has no id and the queue never talks to SQS.
check_questions: Does `LoanEvent` carry the id that the consumer needs to dedup?
Does `transition` accept all moves that callers attempt?

findings.title: Events have no id and nothing dedups them
findings.detail: `LoanEvent` has only `type`, `loan_id` and `on`. The consumer (`consumer.py:18`) keeps no record of handled events. SQS delivers at least once and retries a whole failed batch, so the same mail can be sent again.
findings.suggestion: Add an `id` (for example a uuid) to `LoanEvent` and make the consumer skip ids it has handled.
findings.effect: Redelivered or retried SQS messages mail members again.

findings.title: Queue.publish never sends to SQS
findings.detail: `publish` only appends to a list. No SQS client or `LOAN_EVENTS_URL` read exists in any `.py` file. In the deployed front desk, events stay in process memory and the consumer never receives any.
findings.suggestion: Add an SQS-backed Queue that reads `LOAN_EVENTS_URL` and calls `send_message`, and use it in production.
findings.effect: In production no event reaches the consumer Lambda.

findings.title: give_back changes status outside the state machine
findings.detail: `LoanStore.give_back` sets `returned_on` directly. `api.give_back` also publishes no `loan.returned`. The criterion says status changes go through `status.py` only. The code was there before the PR, but the PR's `transition` contains `RETURNED` handling that nothing calls.
findings.effect: Returns publish no event and skip the transition rules.

transitions.guard: status_of is already OVERDUE on the day

steps.title: Reminders producer
steps.why_it_matters: This is where reminder and overdue events are produced, and where the mail could be sent twice or fail.
steps.explanation: `send_reminders` now calls `transition` per loan, which publishes `loan.reminded`, but it still mails directly. `publish_overdue` is new and calls `transition(OVERDUE)` for loans due yesterday.
check_questions: Does `send_reminders` still send mail directly, and does the consumer send it again?
What does `status_of` return for a loan due yesterday, and does `move` allow that?

suggestions.text: The mail is sent before `transition`, so if the transition raises, the member is mailed but nothing is recorded or published.

findings.title: Reminder mail is sent twice
findings.detail: `send_reminders` still calls `mailer.send` at line 21, then `transition` publishes `loan.reminded`, which `consumer.handle` also mails. The first send has no counterpart removal in the diff. The test only checks the direct outbox, so it does not show this.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `mailer.send` call and its `mailer` parameter from `send_reminders`, so only the consumer mails.
findings.effect: Each member gets two reminder mails per loan, from two components.
preconditions: the SQS delivery works (once the queue is wired)

findings.title: publish_overdue always raises ValueError
findings.detail: The loans selected are due yesterday. `status_of(loan, day)` returns OVERDUE for them because `due_on < on`. `transition` then calls `move(OVERDUE, OVERDUE)`, which is absent from `MOVES[OVERDUE] = {RETURNED}`. So the first loan raises `ValueError` and no overdue event is published.
findings.suggestion: Compute the current status as of the day before, or let `transition` take the loan's status without deriving it from the new date.
findings.effect: No loan.overdue event is ever published, and the job fails on the first late loan.

steps.title: Reminder consumer
steps.why_it_matters: The consumer is supposed to be the only mail sender and to be idempotent.
steps.explanation: `handler` reads SQS records, parses the body and mails the member for `loan.reminded` and `loan.overdue`. For reminded, it also sets `reminded_on` on the loan it loaded from `api.store`.
check_questions: Can the consumer find the loan in a separate Lambda, given `api.store`?
Is anything done about duplicates or a bad record in a batch of 10?

suggestions.text: One failing record raises out of the loop, and the whole batch is retried, which re-sends mails already sent in the batch.

findings.title: Consumer reads loans from an empty per-process store
findings.detail: `api.store` is a `LoanStore` created in `api.py` that holds loans in a dict in memory. In the deployed consumer Lambda that dict is a separate, empty one from the front desk's, so `store.get` raises `KeyError` for every message.
findings.suggestion: Back the store with shared persistence, or put the mail data (email, book, member, due date) into the event.
findings.effect: Every SQS message fails and is retried, and no mail is sent.
preconditions: the Lambdas are deployed as separate functions, as in `template.yaml`

findings.title: Consumer changes loan status outside status.py
findings.detail: The `loan.reminded` branch sets `loan.reminded_on = today()`. `transition` already sets it when it publishes, and the criterion says only `status.py` changes status.
findings.suggestion: Remove this line, since the producer's `transition` already sets `reminded_on`.
findings.effect: A second place changes status, and the date can differ from the event's `on`.

steps.title: Front desk handler
steps.why_it_matters: The front desk Lambda now imports the consumer and sends mail itself, which contradicts the split.
steps.explanation: `handler.py` imports `consumer` and adds `POST /remind`. That route calls `consumer.handle` directly, skips the queue and skips the state machine, then answers 202.
check_questions: Does importing `consumer` break the 'share only events' rule?
What happens on `/remind` for a missing body or unknown loan id?

suggestions.text: A missing `id` or an unknown loan raises `KeyError`, which becomes a 500, and the 202 would be wrong anyway because the mail is sent synchronously.

findings.title: Front desk imports the consumer module
findings.detail: `from library import api, consumer` ties the front desk to the consumer, which in turn imports `api`, `dates` and `mailer`. The two Lambdas are meant to share the events module and nothing else.
findings.suggestion: Remove the import and do not call consumer code from the front desk.
findings.effect: The two Lambdas cannot be built or deployed separately, and changes to the consumer affect the front desk.

findings.title: /remind mails from the front desk and skips the state machine
findings.detail: The route calls `consumer.handle` directly, so the front desk Lambda sends the mail. No `transition` runs and no event is published. The route also returns 202 and `reminded: true` although the mail was sent synchronously.
findings.suggestion: Call `transition(loan, Status.REMINDED, queue, today())` and let the consumer send the mail.
findings.effect: The front desk becomes a second mail sender, and the loan's status changes without an event.

steps.title: SAM template
steps.why_it_matters: The template decides what is deployed, with which permissions and secrets, and how SQS failures are handled.
steps.explanation: Defines the queue, the front desk Lambda with send permission and `LOAN_EVENTS_URL`, and the consumer Lambda with an SQS trigger (batch size 10). Nothing sets `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN`, a dead-letter queue, or batch failure reporting.
check_questions: Where does `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN` come from in the deployed function?
What happens to a message that keeps failing?

findings.title: FRONT_DESK_TOKEN is not set, so the token is empty
findings.detail: `handler.py` reads `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN` with default `""`, and the template sets only `LOAN_EVENTS_URL`. With an empty token, `hmac.compare_digest("", "")` passes for a header of `Bearer ` with nothing after it. The new `/remind` route then lets that caller trigger mail. Whether the gateway passes such a header is not visible.
findings.suggestion: Set `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN` from a secret parameter, and make the handler reject an empty configured token.
findings.effect: An unauthenticated caller could use `/late` and `/remind`.
preconditions: `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN` is not provided in another way at deploy time
the HttpApi forwards an `authorization: Bearer ` header with an empty token
findings.path_why: assumed: depends on the gateway passing an empty bearer value through and on how the variable is set at deploy time

findings.title: Consumer has no DLQ and no partial-batch failure handling
findings.detail: The queue has no `RedrivePolicy` and the event source has no `FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures]`. The consumer raises on a bad record, so the whole batch of 10 is retried and mailed again, and a poison message is retried until retention ends.
findings.suggestion: Add a dead-letter queue and `ReportBatchItemFailures`, and return the failed item ids from the consumer.
findings.effect: One bad record causes repeated duplicate mails and endless retries.

findings.title: Both functions have no CodeUri, so they deploy the same package
findings.detail: Neither function sets `CodeUri`, so both are built from the same directory with the whole `library` package. This keeps the two Lambdas from sharing only the events module.
findings.suggestion: Give each function its own `CodeUri`, with only the code it needs plus the shared events module.
findings.effect: The front desk package contains the consumer and vice versa.
preconditions: the SAM build uses the default root directory for both functions

steps.title: Tests
steps.why_it_matters: The tests pass while the double mail, the failing overdue job and the missing dedup are all in the code.
steps.explanation: Adds a consumer test for one reminded event, an event test for `transition`, and adapts `test_reminders` to the new `queue` argument. They do not cover the acceptance criteria.
check_questions: Does any test count mails when both `send_reminders` and the consumer run?
Is `publish_overdue` or a duplicate event tested?

findings.title: No test for exactly one mail, overdue, or dedup
findings.detail: `test_reminds_two_days_before_due_once` only checks the outbox of the direct send and never looks at `queue`. `publish_overdue` has no test, and `test_consumer.py` has no duplicate-event or overdue case. So the double mail, the `ValueError` in `publish_overdue` and the missing dedup would all go unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Add tests that run `send_reminders` and the consumer on its queue messages and assert one mail, test `publish_overdue`, and feed the same event twice.
findings.effect: The acceptance criteria can break without a failing test.

asks.text: Every status change goes through the state machine in status.py only, publishing one event per change
asks.why: The consumer sets `reminded_on`, `/remind` and `LoanStore.give_back` bypass `transition`, and `publish_overdue` raises.

asks.text: The reminder consumer is the only component that sends reminder and overdue mails
asks.short: Consumer is the only mail sender
asks.why: `send_reminders` still calls `mailer.send`, and the front desk `/remind` calls `consumer.handle`.

asks.text: The front desk Lambda and the consumer are deployed separately and share only the events module
asks.why: `handler.py` imports `consumer`, and the template builds both from the same code.

asks.text: Each event carries an id and the consumer skips an event it has already handled
asks.why: `LoanEvent` has no id and `consumer.handle` has no seen-ids check.

asks.text: A member still gets exactly one reminder mail two days before a loan is due
asks.why: The direct `mailer.send` and the consumer both mail for the same loan.

asks.text: Reminder and overdue mails move out of the request path: status change publishes to a queue and a consumer Lambda mails
asks.why: `Queue.publish` is a list and never sends to SQS, and the consumer's store is empty in its own Lambda.

asks.text: A new POST /remind route on the front desk that mails one loan at once
asks.why: The description does not mention it, and it sends mail from the front desk, against the PR's own goals.

adds: `template.yaml` with two functions and a queue.
changes: `send_reminders` now takes a queue and calls `transition`, but still mails directly.
The front desk handler gets `POST /remind` and imports the consumer.
runtime: A status change should publish to SQS, but the queue is an in-memory list.
The consumer Lambda reads from an in-memory store of its own.

intent.text: Move reminder and overdue mails out of the request path by publishing events and mailing from a consumer.
All status changes go through `transition`, which publishes one event.
Add a consumer Lambda triggered by SQS.

behavior_points.text: The front desk can trigger a reminder mail through `POST /remind`.
The consumer mails members for `loan.reminded` and `loan.overdue` events.

checked.note: event has no id; Queue not SQS
